question: When species newly enter the wet active route, do they appear across larger geographic spans within the route than expected under the existing activation nulls?
population: Frozen NAAMP matched pairs restricted to pairs with identical nonmissing SiteID at all ten StopNumbers and valid pinned Coordinates.csv coordinates for all ten physical stops.

endpoints.total_route_new_span_km: For each species absent from the entire dry route but present in the wet route, calculate maximum great-circle distance between its occupied wet stops; single-stop species have span 0. Sum spans across route-new species.
endpoints.mean_route_new_span_km: Mean of the same species-level spans across all route-new species in the pair; 0 if no route-new species.
endpoints.multi_stop_route_new_species: Number of route-new species detected at >=2 wet stops, reported as a link to the previous spread diagnostic.

model: Use the frozen matched-pair design residual for each endpoint; compare observed rain-contrast coefficients with 1,000 simulations under the same kappa=2 uniform activation null and a=0.75 persistence-preserving null.
primary_prediction: Broad route-scale activation is supported only if total_route_new_span_km exceeds the upper 95% null bound under both nulls AND mean_route_new_span_km exceeds the upper 95% null bound under both nulls.
coverage_gate: >=3500 physically stable pairs with complete ten-stop coordinates and >=450 routes; otherwise no primary classification.
interpretation: A positive result supports route-scale synchronous activation, not movement of individuals among stops.
Large spans can reflect broad atmospheric, reproductive or hydrological cues; this test does not distinguish among them.
Failure does not prove purely local recruitment.
No causal rainfall claim and no RC11 submission change are authorized.
